answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a slashable identity bond. Each agent locks capital tied to one verified credential, and voting weight scales with that bond. A thousand fake wallets at the wharf gain nothing: funding every one makes the cost rise linearly with each new identity. Peers catch double-voting and burn the stake, so the payoff only reaches its zenith when honest work beats cheating. That forfeiture makes the bond a beacon of commitment: the more a farmer spends on fake accounts, the more it risks losing, so mass impersonation stays unprofitable.
